title: Guard's rules.toml edit-path drops all_constraints parse errors
description:
Surfaced by the Codex review of sutra/289.

The guard's `.sutra/rules.toml` edit-time branch (src/bin/guard.rs:189-204) runs only `check_proposed_rules_ratchet`. That function (src/guard.rs:841) parses the proposed rules and calls `all_constraints`, but discards the parse errors: `let (constraints, _errors) = parsed.all_constraints();`. The branch then early-returns.

Consequence: when a user edits `.sutra/rules.toml`, no `ConstraintParseError` is surfaced at edit time — not the removed-`[conventions]`-block warning added in sutra/289, nor any other parse error (unknown constraint kind, invalid glob, etc.). These only appear later through the MCP tools (constraints list / orient / review), which do include `constraint_parse_errors`.

This is a pre-existing limitation (the branch was always ratchet-only), not a regression from sutra/289 — but it undercuts the intent of that task's criterion 2 ("existing workspaces are told rather than ignored") at the one moment the workspace is most likely editing its rules.toml.

Scope: surface `all_constraints` parse errors in the guard's rules.toml edit path. Parse errors are advisory, so warn (stderr eprintln, like the advisory pattern/pubspec findings already do) rather than deny. Options: add a small `guard::proposed_rules_parse_errors(proposed) -> Vec<String>` helper and print in the branch, OR change `check_proposed_rules_ratchet` to return the errors alongside violations (heavier — audit callers, this repo's refactor-contract discipline applies).

Acceptance:
- Editing `.sutra/rules.toml` to add a `[conventions]` block emits a warning at guard edit time naming the block as removed.
- Other rules.toml parse errors (unknown kind, invalid glob) are also surfaced at edit time.
- A guard test drives a proposed `[conventions]` block through the entry point and fails if the warning is dropped.
- Parse errors warn, not deny (advisory severity).
execution_record: Took the lighter of the two suggested options: added guard::proposed_rules_parse_errors(proposed) -> Vec<String> (re-parses + runs all_constraints, maps errors to rendered strings) rather than changing check_proposed_rules_ratchet's return type (which would have required auditing all callers under refactor-contract discipline). Bin branch prints each via eprintln (stderr) before the ratchet check — confirmed by anchored lesson 019f8a82 that a PreToolUse hook may emit only one JSON object on stdout, so advisory output must use stderr. 4 unit tests: conventions block, unknown kind, valid rules (no warn), malformed TOML (silent bail). Went as planned.
root_cause: The guard's .sutra/rules.toml edit-time branch (src/bin/guard.rs) ran only check_proposed_rules_ratchet, which parses proposed rules via all_constraints but discards the returned parse errors (let (constraints, _errors) = ...) and early-returns. So no ConstraintParseError was ever surfaced at edit time — parse errors only reached the user later through the MCP tools' constraint_parse_errors. Pre-existing limitation, not a sutra/289 regression.
